types.name: Fenrir::BallJoint
types.doc: Holds the two frames' positions together and lets the bodies turn freely about them.

types.name: Fenrir::BoxShape
types.doc: A box centred on its entity, `halfExtents` from the centre to each face before the entity's scale, which applies per axis. Its edges are rounded slightly (by at most 0.05, less for a thin box).

types.name: Fenrir::CapsuleShape
types.doc: A capsule centred on its entity and standing along its local y axis: a cylinder `2 * halfHeight` tall, capped by hemispheres of `radius`, so `2 * (halfHeight + radius)` tall in all. Scale stretches `halfHeight` by the entity's y scale and `radius` by the larger of its x and z scales.

types.name: Fenrir::Entity
types.doc: Entity class that is used to interact with the entity list. This forms the basis of the ECS

types.name: Fenrir::GroundState
types.doc: What a character body stood on at the end of its last move.

values.name: OnGround
values.doc: Standing on walkable ground: no steeper than its `maxSlope`.

values.name: OnSteepGround
values.doc: Standing on ground steeper than its `maxSlope`.

values.name: Touching
values.doc: Touching something, a wall or a ledge, with nothing underneath.

types.name: Fenrir::CharacterState
types.doc: How a character body's last move left it: written by physics into CharacterBody::state after every move, against the bodies' poses before that tick's step. Game code's edits to it are overwritten.

fields.name: groundBody
fields.doc: The body entity of the ground (a rigid body or a character body), on ground only; empty otherwise.

fields.name: groundCollider
fields.doc: The collider entity of the ground touched, on ground only; empty otherwise.

fields.name: groundPoint
fields.doc: World space, where the character touches its ground, on ground only.

fields.name: groundNormal
fields.doc: World space, unit length, up from the ground, averaged over the ground contacts, on ground only. Each is the normal of the face touched, which is also how its steepness is judged: a box's rounded edge counts as the face it rounds, so a step's edge is not steep ground.

fields.name: groundVelocity
fields.doc: m/s, the ground's velocity at the character, on ground only. Physics adds it to the next move on walkable ground, never to `velocity`.

fields.name: groundAngularVelocity
fields.doc: rad/s, world space, the ground's angular velocity, on ground only. Physics never turns the character with its ground: game code that wants it turned with a turntable turns it by this.

fields.name: movedVelocity
fields.doc: m/s, the last move's displacement over the tick's time: how fast the character actually moved, which `velocity` (trimmed, and never measured from displacement) does not say.

fields.name: carriedVelocity
fields.doc: m/s, the whole velocity of the walkable ground the character left (walking or jumping off), added to each move and trimmed by what it hits, as `velocity` is, until it lands. A teleport clears it. It is never in `velocity`; `movedVelocity` includes it.

fields.name: onWall
fields.doc: Touching a wall at the end of the move: a surface too steep to stand on that is not its ground.

fields.name: onCeiling
fields.doc: Touching a ceiling at the end of the move: a surface facing down.

fields.name: shapeBlocked
fields.doc: The Collider's shape or scale does not fit where the character is yet: it keeps the old one.

types.name: Fenrir::CharacterBody
types.doc:
Makes the entity's own Collider a character body (ADR-0014): collide-and-slide, moved by `velocity`, and seen by other bodies, queries and triggers as a kinematic body of its shape, naming its entity. There is no move call: game code writes `velocity` in `Tick`, and physics moves the character by it once in `PostTick`, before the step, characters one at a time in entity order.

`velocity` is input and output, like RigidBody::linearVelocity. After the move physics writes it back with the parts that went into what the character touches removed: ground takes only the falling part, and a wall or ceiling the part going into it. Landing clears falling speed and a ceiling clears upward speed. It is never measured from displacement, so game code wanting the speed it asked for keeps its own copy, and `state.movedVelocity` is how fast the character actually moved. Gravity is game code's: physics adds none, so add `PhysicsWorld::Gravity() * dt` each tick, and set `velocity.y` to jump.

Walking: velocity into ground steeper than `maxSlope` is cancelled, so it is not climbed; steps up to `stepHeight` are walked up, and the character sticks to the ground up to `floorSnap` below it walking down slopes and steps. A step-up or a ground snap never shows in `velocity`, only in `state.movedVelocity`. Standing on a walkable slope it stays put, unless `stopOnSlope` is off: then the falling part of `velocity` slides it downhill, but only if game code adds its input to the written-back velocity; setting the horizontal speed every tick throws the slide's speed away, and the character only creeps.

A character rides the walkable ground it stands on, a lift, a shuttle, a raft or a turntable, with no game code: the ground's velocity at the character is added to its move, never to `velocity`, which is trimmed in the ground's frame, so a descending lift's speed is never taken for falling. Steep ground is not ridden. Leaving the ground keeps its velocity as `state.carriedVelocity` until landing. Moving before the step, a character trails a descending platform by one tick of travel (2.5 cm at 1.5 m/s), still on the ground; where a lift turns from down to up, that gap leaves it in the air for 1 to 4 ticks.

Its shape is the Collider on its entity, whose PhysicsMaterial and CollisionFilter apply to it as to any body; that Collider makes no static body. The Transform sits at the collider's centre. Physics writes back only the position; the shape takes the entity's full world rotation, and up is always world +Y.

Writing the Transform's world position (moving its parent included) teleports the character: no sweep, its contacts and `state` found from that tick's move where it now is, `velocity` kept, and no blend across the jump. Writing only its rotation turns the shape where it stands, with no sweep, and is not a teleport: it blends, and the next move pushes the shape out of anything it now overlaps. Turn it in `Tick`, as a kinematic body is moved. A parented character moves in world space: its local Transform is written back against its parent's world transform, parents before children.

It is inactive beside a RigidBody (which works instead, its Collider then the RigidBody's), with no Collider, or with a MeshShape: the component is kept, one warning is logged each time it becomes so, and it is a character again by itself once it can be. A solid collider on a child entity with no RigidBody of its own is not part of the character and makes no body, with one warning; a child Trigger works as beneath any body, and the character never sets it off. A joint naming a character is inactive. While disabled or inactive, nothing is written back but `state`, which reads as the defaults.

Other bodies: a move that hits a dynamic body pushes it towards the character's speed at the contact, aiming at 0.9 × the closing speed (so a light box keeps pace and is never launched), with at most `pushForce` on each body and never downward; static and kinematic bodies are not pushed. A move that ends on ground presses the ground body with `mass` under the world's gravity, scaled by how the ground faces it, so a character tips a seesaw or sinks a raft. Both act in the step after the move. A dynamic body never pushes a character: it meets the character as an immovable wall and stops or bounces off, and knockback is game code writing `velocity`. A kinematic body (a door, a paddle) moving into a character shoves it at exactly the body's speed, whatever its `mass`, and that speed shows in the written-back `velocity` until game code overwrites it. Stated limits: a fast kinematic body may overlap a character for a tick until the next move pushes it out; a character caught between a kinematic body and a wall is not crushed or detected, but stays overlapped and stuck (`state.onWall` and the contacts show it); and a body resting on a character (a box on its head) is not carried along, but slips or is pushed out, though a jump still pushes it up.

Bodies, queries and triggers meet a character as a kinematic body of its shape, named by its entity as body and collider: triggers report it during the step, `QueryFilter::ignoreBody` skips it, and hits carry no character flag. Its entity's CollisionFilter filters both what meets it and its own moves, under the one symmetric rule, so a character ignoring a layer walks through that layer's bodies, and those bodies, triggers and queries pass through it; its entity's PhysicsMaterial is what bodies hitting or resting on it feel, and never changes how it moves. Edits to either apply from the next tick. Characters block each other and neither pushes the other: one standing on another rides it (`state.groundBody` names it), and one standing on this character never holds it down, so a jump lifts it. In entity order, a character's move meets the others where their last moves left them.

fields.name: velocity
fields.doc: World space, m/s, read fresh every tick and written back trimmed by what the character touches.

fields.name: maxSlope
fields.doc: Radians (45°): ground steeper than this is not walkable. 0 turns slope limiting off.

fields.name: stepHeight
fields.doc: Metres: the highest step the character walks up. 0 turns stair walking off.

fields.name: floorSnap
fields.doc: Metres: how far down the character sticks to the ground walking down slopes and steps. 0 turns it off.

fields.name: pushForce
fields.doc: Newtons: the most force a move's push applies to each dynamic body it hits. 0 turns pushing off.

fields.name: mass
fields.doc: Kilograms: only the character's weight on its ground; it does not change pushing or being pushed. 0 turns it off.

fields.name: stopOnSlope
fields.doc: On walkable ground, the falling part of `velocity` does not slide the character down a slope.

fields.name: interpolate
fields.doc: As RigidBody::interpolate: between ticks the Transform holds its position and rotation blended between the last two steps, stair step-ups and ground snaps included, while `Tick` systems see the true one. A teleport and a new character snap. PhysicsConfig can turn interpolation off for every character.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Disabled: not moved, invisible to bodies, queries and triggers, `velocity` and the Transform left to game code, and `state` reset. Enabled again, it finds its contacts and ground where it is that tick, as a teleport does, and is not blended from where it was.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: Read-back: overwritten by physics after every move.

types.name: Fenrir::CollisionMesh
types.doc: A handle to a collision mesh: vertex and index data FenrirPhysics cooked once (Physics::CreateCollisionMesh) and colliders share. Plain data; copying it does not keep the mesh alive. Valid until released (Physics::ReleaseCollisionMesh); a released handle is never handed out again. The default handle refers to no mesh.

types.name: Fenrir::ConvexHullShape
types.doc: The convex hull of a collision mesh's vertices (its indices are not used), placed on its entity as the vertices are placed about the origin. Scale is applied per axis, mirroring included.

types.name: Fenrir::MeshShape
types.doc:
A collision mesh's triangles, as they are placed about the origin. Scale is applied per axis, mirroring included. Triangles collide on their front face only (counter-clockwise when seen from in front).

A triangle mesh has no volume: on a dynamic body it is weighed as the solid box of its bounds, and two triangle meshes never collide with each other. Prefer it for static level geometry, and a hull for anything that moves.

types.name: Fenrir::ShapeType
types.doc: Which kind of shape a CollisionShape holds.

types.name: Fenrir::SphereShape
types.doc: A sphere centred on its entity. A non-uniform scale is replaced by its largest component.

types.name: Fenrir::CollisionShape
types.doc:
A collision shape: exactly one kind of shape and its dimensions, by value (ADR-0011).

Assign a kind to change it (`collider.shape = SphereShape{1.0f}`); read or edit the dimensions through the checked view (`collider.shape.As<BoxShape>().halfExtents.y = 2.0f`). Reading it as a kind it does not hold asserts.

types.name: Fenrir::Collider
types.doc:
Gives the entity collision geometry, placed at its world transform and scaled by its world scale. One per entity. It belongs to the body of the nearest of its entity and that entity's ancestors with a RigidBody; without one the collider is static, unless its own entity has a CharacterBody, which makes it that character's shape. Adding, removing or moving a collider beneath a body rebuilds that body's shape on the next tick.

The scale is baked into the backend's shape, so changing the shape's dimensions or the entity's scale rebuilds that shape on the next tick: fine occasionally, costly every tick. Each kind's shape documents how it takes a non-uniform scale. A box, sphere or capsule is never thinner than 0.001 in any dimension once scaled (a zero size is clamped to that). Colliders whose box, sphere or capsule is identical once scaled share one backend shape.

types.name: Fenrir::CollisionFilter
types.doc:
Which of the 32 collision layers a body is in, and which layers it collides with. Optional: a body without one is in layer 0 and collides with every layer.

Two bodies collide when each one's mask includes a layer of the other: `(a.layers & b.mask) != 0 && (b.layers & a.mask) != 0`. It is read from the body's entity and applies to all the body's colliders; one on a child collider of a compound body is ignored, with a warning. Edits take effect on the next tick. Layers can be given names in PhysicsConfig, and looked up through CollisionLayers.

fields.name: layers
fields.doc: The layers the body is in, one bit per layer (layer `i` is `1u << i`).

fields.name: mask
fields.doc: The layers the body collides with, one bit per layer.

types.name: Fenrir::Contact
types.doc: One contact of a body, as PhysicsWorld::ForEachContact reports it.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The body entity (a rigid body or a character body) asked about.

fields.name: collider
fields.doc: The collider entity of `body` touching: `body` itself, or one beneath it in a compound body.

fields.name: otherBody
fields.doc: The body entity (a rigid body or a character body) `body` touches.

fields.name: otherCollider
fields.doc: The collider entity of `otherBody` touching.

fields.name: point
fields.doc: Where they touch, in world space, as of the last step.

fields.name: normal
fields.doc: World space, unit length, pointing from `body` to `otherBody`, as of the last step.

types.name: Fenrir::ContactBegin
types.doc:
Two solid colliders of different bodies began touching (a contact), and at least one of the bodies has an enabled ContactEvents.

A and B are ordered by entity id, `bodyA` first. A body falling asleep does not end a contact.

A character is named as both body and collider. Its contacts with static and kinematic bodies and other characters are found by its moves, before the step; with dynamic bodies, also by its body in the step, so a ball that bounces off between two moves is still reported. Either way, one pair of entities makes one contact.

fields.name: bodyA
fields.doc: The body entity (a rigid body or a character body) of A, the lower entity id.

fields.name: bodyB
fields.doc: The body entity (a rigid body or a character body) of B.

fields.name: colliderA
fields.doc: A's collider entity touching: `bodyA` itself, or one beneath it in a compound body.

fields.name: colliderB
fields.doc: B's collider entity touching: `bodyB` itself, or one beneath it in a compound body.

fields.name: point
fields.doc: Where they touch, in world space.

fields.name: normal
fields.doc: World space, unit length, pointing from A to B.

fields.name: relativeSpeed
fields.doc: How fast A and B were closing along `normal` when they began touching, in metres per second.

types.name: Fenrir::ContactEnd
types.doc: A contact reported by ContactBegin ended: the colliders separated, one of the bodies or colliders was removed, or ContactEvents was removed or disabled on both bodies. Names the same entities, in the same order, as its ContactBegin.

fields.name: bodyA
fields.doc: The body entity (a rigid body or a character body) of A, as in its ContactBegin.

fields.name: bodyB
fields.doc: The body entity (a rigid body or a character body) of B, as in its ContactBegin.

fields.name: colliderA
fields.doc: A's collider entity, as in its ContactBegin.

fields.name: colliderB
fields.doc: B's collider entity, as in its ContactBegin.

types.name: Fenrir::ContactEvents
types.doc: Reports the body's contacts as ContactBegin and ContactEnd events. Put it on the body entity (a rigid body or a character body).

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Disabled, the body's contacts are not reported; disabling it ends those reported on the next step, unless the other body reports them.

types.name: Fenrir::JointSpring
types.doc: How hard a part of a joint pulls back.

fields.name: frequency
fields.doc: Hertz: 0 is rigid. Negative is treated as 0, and above half the tick rate is lowered to it.

fields.name: damping
fields.doc: The damping ratio: 1 is critical. Negative is treated as 0.

types.name: Fenrir::DistanceJoint
types.doc: Keeps the two frames' positions between `minDistance` and `maxDistance` apart, and ignores the frames' rotations: a rod at min == max, a rope at min 0, a spring when soft.

fields.name: minDistance
fields.doc: Metres. Negative is raised to 0, with a warning.

fields.name: maxDistance
fields.doc: Metres. Below `minDistance` is raised to it, with a warning.

fields.name: spring
fields.doc: Makes the distance soft: it stretches beyond the range and springs back.

types.name: Fenrir::FixedJoint
types.doc: Holds the two frames together in position and rotation: the bodies move as one.

types.name: Fenrir::JointLimits
types.doc:
The range a hinge or slider is kept in, measured from the rest pose. Disabled, it is free.

The rest pose lies inside the range (min <= 0 <= max): a range excluding it, or with min above max, is widened to take in both ends and the rest pose, with a warning. min == max holds the joint at the rest pose. A hinge's limits lie within a half turn either way, and are lowered to it with a warning.

A hard limit (a rigid spring) always beats the joint's motor, however strong. A soft limit is a spring, which a motor or a blow may push past.

fields.name: min
fields.doc: Radians for a hinge, metres for a slider.

fields.name: max
fields.doc: Radians for a hinge, metres for a slider.

fields.name: spring
fields.doc: Makes the limit soft.

types.name: Fenrir::JointMotorMode
types.doc: What a motor drives: nothing, a velocity or a position.

types.name: Fenrir::JointMotor
types.doc: Drives a hinge's angle or a slider's offset, measured from the rest pose. A hard limit always stops it.

fields.name: targetVelocity
fields.doc: Radians or metres per second, read in Velocity mode only.

fields.name: targetPosition
fields.doc: Radians or metres, read in Position mode only. Outside an enabled limit, it is taken as the limit.

fields.name: maxForce
fields.doc: Newton metres for a hinge, newtons for a slider, either way. Negative is treated as 0.

fields.name: spring
fields.doc: How hard Position mode drives.

types.name: Fenrir::HingeJoint
types.doc: Holds the two frames together but for turning about their shared X axis. The hinge angle is signed by the right-hand rule about frameA's X: it is frameB's turn relative to frameA, so it follows which body is A.

fields.name: limits
fields.doc: Radians.

fields.name: friction
fields.doc: The most torque, in newton metres, resisting the hinge's turn while its motor is off: a door stays where it is left. Negative is treated as 0.

types.name: Fenrir::JointFrame
types.doc: A pose on a body: local to the body entity's origin, or in world space for the world end of a joint. Its position follows the body's world scale (an anchor on a crate's corner stays on the corner); its rotation does not. Its local X axis is a hinge's axis, a slider's direction and a swing-twist joint's twist axis.

types.name: Fenrir::JointType
types.doc: Which kind of joint a JointKind holds.

types.name: Fenrir::SliderJoint
types.doc: Holds the two frames together but for sliding along their shared X axis, without turning.

fields.name: limits
fields.doc: Metres.

fields.name: friction
fields.doc: The most force, in newtons, resisting the slide while its motor is off. Negative is treated as 0.

types.name: Fenrir::SwingTwistMotor
types.doc: Drives a swing-twist joint's rotation, swing and twist together. Its cone and twist limits always stop it.

fields.name: targetRotation
fields.doc: frameB's rotation relative to frameA, read in Position mode only: the identity is the rest pose. Outside the cone or the twist range, it is taken as the nearest rotation inside them.

fields.name: targetAngularVelocity
fields.doc: Radians per second in frameA's axes, read in Velocity mode only.

fields.name: maxTorque
fields.doc: Newton metres, about each axis. Negative is treated as 0.

fields.name: spring
fields.doc: How hard Position mode drives.

types.name: Fenrir::SwingTwistJoint
types.doc:
Holds the two frames' positions together and keeps frameB's turn relative to frameA within hard limits, in radians: a swing about Y and Z within a cone about frameA's X, and a twist about X within a range. A shoulder or a hip.

The swing limits are cone half-angles from 0 to a half turn (a half turn frees that swing), moved into that range with a warning. The twist range lies within a half turn either way and takes in the rest pose, corrected with a warning as JointLimits are.

fields.name: swingYLimit
fields.doc: The cone's half-angle about Y.

fields.name: swingZLimit
fields.doc: The cone's half-angle about Z.

fields.name: friction
fields.doc: The most torque, in newton metres, resisting the joint's turn while its motor is off. Negative is treated as 0.

types.name: Fenrir::JointKind
types.doc:
A joint kind: exactly one kind of joint and its settings, by value, as CollisionShape holds a shape.

Assign a kind to change it (`joint.kind = HingeJoint{}`); read or edit its settings through the checked view (`joint.kind.As<HingeJoint>()`). Reading it as a kind it does not hold asserts.

types.name: Fenrir::Joint
types.doc:
Joins two bodies, or a body and the world (ADR-0013). Put it on a joint entity: any entity, one of the bodies it joins included. Physics never reads the joint entity's Transform. A body takes part in any number of joints, each on its own entity.

The rest pose is where the two frames coincide in world space; physics never captures frames from the scene. Use FrameFromWorld to author them: frames written by hand on a scaled or parented body are easy to get wrong.

Plain data, which physics compares each tick with what it last applied (ADR-0011). `enabled`, `collideConnected`, the break thresholds and every setting of the kind (limits, motors, springs, friction) are live edits, applied on the next tick. Changing the kind, a body, a frame or a body's scale recreates the joint in the backend: cheap, but one step softer while it settles. Every change wakes both bodies.

Out-of-range settings are corrected as physics applies them, with one warning per joint for each kind of mistake; the component keeps what was written.

A joint is inactive while `bodyA` is empty, both bodies are the same entity, or either names something that is not a body entity of the joint entity's scene (destroyed, never a body, a compound body's child collider, a trigger, or in another scene). It does nothing, with one warning each time it goes inactive, wakes the body left, and works again by itself once both names are bodies. A joint whose bodies are all static or kinematic is idle, not inactive: kept silently, it holds once one becomes dynamic. Motion-type changes keep a joint as it is.

Writing one body's Transform, or reparenting it, teleports it alone: the other body stays where it is, and the joint pulls the two back together over the next steps, by position, so a teleport adds no velocity to them and never breaks the joint (one left out of a resting pose, or past the joint's limits, still falls while it is pulled back). How fast they come together is not promised. To move a jointed group as one, write each of its bodies' Transforms in the same tick; there is no group teleport. A kinematic body's moves are not teleports. Editing a body's colliders (their shapes, or the child colliders of a compound body added, removed or moved) keeps its joints' frames where they are on it, wherever its centre of mass goes.

fields.name: bodyA
fields.doc: A body entity: a RigidBody's, or a standalone static collider's. Never the world.

fields.name: bodyB
fields.doc: A body entity, or empty: the world.

fields.name: frameA
fields.doc: Local to bodyA's origin.

fields.name: frameB
fields.doc: Local to bodyB's origin, or in world space when bodyB is the world.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: A disabled joint holds nothing.

fields.name: collideConnected
fields.doc: Whether the two bodies collide with each other. While the joint is enabled, false keeps every solid collider of one from colliding with the other's; true leaves them to their CollisionFilters, which it never overrides. Only the two bodies named: in a chain, bodies two apart still collide. Triggers and queries ignore it. A live edit.

fields.name: breakForce
fields.doc: Newtons. The first step whose JointState::force is over it, while the joint's bodies are awake, breaks the joint: physics sets `enabled` to false and sends a JointBroken. Infinity (the default) never breaks; negative is treated as 0. Setting `enabled` back to true repairs it.

fields.name: breakTorque
fields.doc: Newton metres: as breakForce, against JointState::torque.

types.name: Fenrir::JointBroken
types.doc:
A joint broke: in the last step its load went over its Joint's `breakForce` or `breakTorque`, so physics set its `enabled` to false. Sent only for breaks, never when game code disables a joint. Sorted by joint entity.

Repair a joint by setting `enabled` back to true: one still over its threshold breaks again on the next step, with another event.

fields.name: joint
fields.doc: The joint entity, whose Joint is now disabled.

fields.name: bodyA
fields.doc: The joint's bodyA.

fields.name: bodyB
fields.doc: The joint's bodyB: empty for the world.

fields.name: force
fields.doc: Newtons, world space: what the joint applied to bodyB in the step that broke it (JointState::force).

fields.name: torque
fields.doc: Newton metres, world space, likewise (JointState::torque).

types.name: Fenrir::JointFrames
types.doc: Both frames of a joint, as FrameFromWorld computes them.

types.name: Fenrir::JointState
types.doc:
How a joint sits and how hard it pulls, as PhysicsWorld::GetJointState reads it from the last completed step.

The pose readings come from the bodies' poses after that step and the joint's frames, for every kind, never from interpolated Transforms. `force` and `torque` sum every part of the joint (holding the frames together, its limits, its motor and friction) over the step's last collision step: approximate within a step, exact enough for steady loads such as a hanging chain's weight.

fields.name: force
fields.doc: Newtons, world space: what the joint applies to bodyB (bodyA gets the negative).

fields.name: torque
fields.doc: Newton metres, world space, about the joint's anchor: what the joint applies to bodyB, likewise.

fields.name: relative
fields.doc: frameB's pose in frameA's axes: the identity is the rest pose. For a swing-twist joint, its rotation is in the same terms as its motor's `targetRotation`.

fields.name: position
fields.doc:
A hinge's angle (radians, wrapped to (-pi, pi], with no count of whole turns), a slider's offset along frameA's X (metres), a distance joint's length (metres); 0 for the other kinds.

A hinge's angle is frameB's turn relative to frameA, so its sign follows which body is A: put the fixed part in bodyA to read a positive opening. A body hinged to the world (always bodyB) reads with the opposite sign.

types.name: Fenrir::MotionType
types.doc: How a rigid body moves: never (static), by game code (kinematic) or by the simulation (dynamic).

types.name: Fenrir::MotorcycleLean
types.doc: How a motorcycle keeps itself up: it leans into turns, and stands at rest.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Disabled, the bike falls over. A live edit.

fields.name: maxAngle
fields.doc: Radians: the most it leans, kept within 0 and a quarter turn. Changing it rebuilds the vehicle privately, keeping the engine speed, the gear and the wheels' spin.

fields.name: limitSteering
fields.doc: Caps steering by speed so the lean stays under `maxAngle`. A live edit.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleEngine
types.doc: A vehicle's engine. Its torque curve is built from the shape fields; the engine never stalls.

fields.name: maxTorque
fields.doc: Newton metres, at `peakTorqueRpm`.

fields.name: minRpm
fields.doc: The idle speed, in RPM.

fields.name: torqueAtMinRpm
fields.doc: The fraction of `maxTorque` at `minRpm`.

fields.name: torqueAtMaxRpm
fields.doc: The fraction of `maxTorque` at `maxRpm`.

fields.name: inertia
fields.doc: kg m².

types.name: Fenrir::TransmissionMode
types.doc: Who changes gear: the gearbox itself, or game code through VehicleInput::gear and `clutch`.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleTransmission
types.doc: A vehicle's gearbox: `gearCount` forward gears spaced geometrically from `firstGear` to `topGear`, and one reverse gear. The shift and switch fields are read only in Automatic.

fields.name: reverseGear
fields.doc: The reverse gear's ratio, as a positive magnitude.

fields.name: shiftUpRpm
fields.doc: RPM.

fields.name: shiftDownRpm
fields.doc: RPM.

fields.name: switchTime
fields.doc: Seconds a shift takes.

fields.name: clutchReleaseTime
fields.doc: Seconds the clutch takes to engage after a shift.

fields.name: switchLatency
fields.doc: Seconds after a shift before the next.

types.name: Fenrir::MotorcycleVehicle
types.doc:
A motorcycle: two wheels in line, leaning into turns and standing at rest by itself through `lean`. The physics backend marks its motorcycles as still in development, so a backend upgrade may change how one leans.

Like a wheeled vehicle, it drives both wheels until game code names differentials: give it one VehicleDifferential naming only its rear wheel to ride like the backend's sample bike.

fields.name: limitedSlipRatio
fields.doc: The limited-slip ratio between differentials.

types.name: Fenrir::MoveCastHit
types.doc: Where a moved shape is blocked (PhysicsWorld::MoveCast).

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The entity of the body that blocked the shape.

fields.name: collider
fields.doc: The entity of the collider that blocked it.

fields.name: point
fields.doc: Where the shape touches the body, on the shape, in world space.

fields.name: normal
fields.doc: The body's surface normal where it was touched, pointing towards the shape.

fields.name: distance
fields.doc: How far the shape can travel along the motion and stay clear of the body: the safe distance.

types.name: Fenrir::OverlapHit
types.doc: A body a shape or point overlaps.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The entity of the body.

fields.name: collider
fields.doc: The entity of the collider.

types.name: Fenrir::PenetrationHit
types.doc: A body a shape overlaps, and how to get out of it (PhysicsWorld::Penetrations).

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The entity of the body.

fields.name: collider
fields.doc: The entity of the collider.

fields.name: point
fields.doc: The shape's deepest point inside the collider, in world space.

fields.name: normal
fields.doc: The unit direction that moves the shape out of the collider along the shortest path.

fields.name: depth
fields.doc: How far along `normal` the shape must move to stop overlapping the collider: more than 0.

types.name: Fenrir::PhysicsMaterial
types.doc:
How a collider's surface responds to contact. Optional: a collider without one has these defaults. Edits take effect on the next tick.

Where two surfaces touch, their friction is the square root of the product of the two frictions, and their restitution the larger of the two restitutions.

A compound body has one surface: the material on its RigidBody's entity, else that of the first of its colliders (in entity order) that has one.

fields.name: friction
fields.doc: How much the surface resists sliding: 0 is ice, about 1 is rubber on concrete.

fields.name: restitution
fields.doc: How much of its speed into a surface a body keeps when it bounces off: 0 does not bounce, 1 bounces back at full speed.

types.name: Fenrir::QueryFilter
types.doc: Which bodies a query can find. Optional: by default a query finds every body except triggers.

fields.name: mask
fields.doc: The collision layers to find, one bit per layer: a body is found if it is in any of them.

fields.name: layers
fields.doc:
The layers the query is in, one bit per layer: when non-zero, a body is found only if its CollisionFilter mask includes one of them, the rule two bodies collide by. 0 (the default) ignores bodies' masks, so a ray still finds a hitbox that collides with nothing.

To find what a body would collide with, filter as it does: `{ .mask = cf.mask, .layers = cf.layers, .ignoreBody = me }`, with `cf` its CollisionFilter (or a default one).

fields.name: ignoreBody
fields.doc: A body never found, such as the one casting the query: the body of this entity (for a child collider's entity, the compound body it belongs to). None by default.

fields.name: hitTriggers
fields.doc: Whether triggers are found.

types.name: Fenrir::RaycastHit
types.doc: Where a ray hit a body.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The entity of the body hit.

fields.name: collider
fields.doc: The entity of the collider hit.

fields.name: point
fields.doc: Where the ray met the surface, in world space.

fields.name: normal
fields.doc: The surface's normal at `point`, pointing out of the body. For a ray that starts inside a body, the opposite of the ray's direction.

fields.name: distance
fields.doc: How far along the ray `point` is: 0 for a ray that starts inside a body.

types.name: Fenrir::RigidBody
types.doc:
Makes the entity's collider a rigid body the physics world simulates (ADR-0011). Plain data: physics finds edits by comparing it, each tick, with what it last applied.

A collider without a RigidBody is static (unless its entity has a CharacterBody, whose shape it is), as is `RigidBody{MotionType::Static}`. Switching `motionType` is a field edit and takes effect on the next tick.

The body's colliders are the one on its own entity and those on entities beneath it that have no RigidBody of their own: a compound body, whose mass is spread over all its colliders. A RigidBody with no collider at all is inactive, with a warning. Removing a RigidBody leaves its colliders static where they are (or part of the body of a RigidBody further up). A dynamic body under a parent simulates in world space: its local `Transform` is written back against its parent's world transform, and moving the parent teleports it. A kinematic or static body follows its world transform when its parent moves. Physics writes a dynamic body's velocities back after each step; writing them sets the body's velocity. A kinematic body is moved by writing its `Transform` (in `Tick`, so physics sees it in `PostTick`); it pushes dynamic bodies and is not pushed.

fields.name: mass
fields.doc: Kilograms. Used by dynamic bodies.

fields.name: linearDamping
fields.doc: How fast linear velocity decays on its own, per second.

fields.name: angularDamping
fields.doc: How fast angular velocity decays on its own, per second.

fields.name: gravityScale
fields.doc: Multiplies the world's gravity for this body.

fields.name: linearVelocity
fields.doc: Metres per second, in world space.

fields.name: angularVelocity
fields.doc: Radians per second about each world axis.

fields.name: interpolate
fields.doc: Whether a dynamic or kinematic body is shown between its last two step poses when a frame ends part of the way through a tick, so it moves smoothly at any frame rate, one step behind the simulation. Between ticks its `Transform` holds the blended pose; `Tick` systems see the true one. Turn it off for a body game code moves every frame, so it does not lag a step. Off, the body is shown at its step pose, even beneath an interpolated parent. PhysicsConfig can turn interpolation off for every body. A vehicle's wheels follow its chassis's.

types.name: Fenrir::ShapeCastHit
types.doc: Where a cast shape hit a body.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The entity of the body hit.

fields.name: collider
fields.doc: The entity of the collider hit.

fields.name: point
fields.doc: Where the cast shape touches the body, on the cast shape, in world space.

fields.name: normal
fields.doc: The body's surface normal where it was hit, pointing towards the cast shape.

fields.name: distance
fields.doc: How far the shape travelled before it touched: 0 for a shape that starts touching.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleTrack
types.doc:
One track of a tracked vehicle: the wheels whose VehicleWheel::track names its side, turning together. Every field is a live edit.

Grip on each surface: `longitudinalFriction` and `lateralFriction` combine with the ground's PhysicsMaterial::friction as a tyre's curve does, as the geometric mean `sqrt(track * ground)`.

fields.name: inertia
fields.doc: kg m²: the track's and its wheels' inertia, as seen on its driven wheel. Kept above 0.

fields.name: maxBrakeTorque
fields.doc: Newton metres at full `brake`.

fields.name: differentialRatio
fields.doc: The gearbox's turns per turn of the track's driven wheel. Kept above 0.

types.name: Fenrir::TrackedVehicle
types.doc:
A tracked vehicle (a tank): two tracks, `left` and `right`, each driven at its own speed ratio, so it steers by VehicleInput::leftTrack and `rightTrack` and pivots on the spot when they are opposite. Game code turns steering into track ratios. It ignores `steer`, `handbrake` and differentials, and its wheels' tyre, brake, steer and inertia fields: its tracks hold its grip, brakes and inertia. Its tracked wheels have no slip.

Each track's driven wheel is its rearmost wheel (the largest chassis-local z), whose radius turns the track's spin into its speed; a track with no wheels does nothing.

types.name: Fenrir::TrailerVehicle
types.doc: A trailer, wagon or hand cart: a vehicle with no engine and no gearbox, towed by an ordinary Joint. It reads VehicleInput's `brake`, `handbrake` and `steer` (for a steered dolly) and ignores `forward`, `gear` and `clutch`, and every VehicleDifferential: its wheels only roll, brake and steer. Its `state` engine and gear fields stay 0.

types.name: Fenrir::Trigger
types.doc:
Makes the entity's collider a trigger: it reports what overlaps it (TriggerEnter, TriggerExit) and never pushes anything.

A trigger follows its entity's world transform, so one under a moving body moves with it, and is in the layers of a CollisionFilter on its own entity (not its body's). It sees static, kinematic and dynamic bodies, sleeping ones included, but not other triggers. A RigidBody on the trigger's own entity gets no solid collider from it. A trigger is never part of a compound body, and ignores the body it is beneath (it would always be inside it).

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: A disabled trigger overlaps nothing: disabling it exits what is inside on the next step.

types.name: Fenrir::TriggerEnter
types.doc: A collider began overlapping an enabled trigger.

fields.name: trigger
fields.doc: The trigger's collider entity.

fields.name: otherBody
fields.doc: The body entity (a rigid body or a character body) of the collider that entered.

fields.name: otherCollider
fields.doc: The collider entity that entered.

types.name: Fenrir::TriggerExit
types.doc: A collider that entered a trigger stopped overlapping it: it left, one of them was removed, or the trigger was disabled. Names the same entities as its TriggerEnter. A body falling asleep inside a trigger does not exit.

fields.name: trigger
fields.doc: The trigger's collider entity, as in its TriggerEnter.

fields.name: otherBody
fields.doc: The body entity (a rigid body or a character body) of the collider that left, as in its TriggerEnter.

fields.name: otherCollider
fields.doc: The collider entity that left, as in its TriggerEnter.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleInput
types.doc: Driver input: what game code sets on a vehicle to drive it, normalised. Game code writes it in `Tick`, and physics applies it in `PostTick`, clamped silently to each field's range. It persists until game code changes it; physics never writes it, so what game code set is what it reads. Any change to it wakes the chassis.

fields.name: forward
fields.doc: [-1, 1]: how hard to drive, negative in reverse (Automatic). In Manual a pedal, [0, 1], the gear setting the direction; a negative value is taken as 0. Trailers ignore it.

fields.name: steer
fields.doc: [-1, 1], + right. Tracked vehicles ignore it.

fields.name: handbrake
fields.doc: [0, 1]. Tracked vehicles ignore it.

fields.name: leftTrack
fields.doc: Tracked only: the left track's speed ratio, [-1, 1]; 0 holds the track still.

fields.name: rightTrack
fields.doc: Tracked only: the right track's speed ratio, [-1, 1]; 0 holds the track still.

fields.name: gear
fields.doc: Manual only: -1 reverse, 0 neutral, 1..n forward, clamped to the gearbox's gears.

fields.name: clutch
fields.doc: Manual only: the clutch pedal, [0, 1], 0 engaged.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleType
types.doc: Which kind of vehicle a VehicleKind holds.

types.name: Fenrir::WheeledVehicle
types.doc: A wheeled vehicle (a car, a truck): steered by turning wheels, driving every wheel equally through its gearbox until game code names differentials.

fields.name: limitedSlipRatio
fields.doc: The limited-slip ratio between differentials.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleKind
types.doc:
A vehicle kind: exactly one kind of vehicle and its drivetrain, by value, as JointKind holds a joint.

Assign a kind to change it (`vehicle.kind = MotorcycleVehicle{}`): a private rebuild that keeps the engine speed, the gear and the wheels' spin. A trailer has no engine or gear to keep, so one turned into another kind starts at idle in neutral, its wheels still spinning. Read or edit its settings through the checked view (`vehicle.kind.As<WheeledVehicle>()`). Reading it as a kind it does not hold asserts.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleProbe
types.doc: How every wheel of a vehicle finds the ground beneath it.

values.name: Ray
values.doc: A ray down the suspension, with a fixed 80° slope limit against the world's up (against gravity).

values.name: Sphere
values.doc: A sphere cast down the suspension, with the same slope limit.

values.name: Cylinder
values.doc: A cylinder the wheel's size cast down the suspension, with no slope limit: wheels roll over kerbs.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleState
types.doc: How the last collision step left a vehicle: written by physics into Vehicle::state after every step. Game code's edits are overwritten. Fields a kind does not have stay 0. A sleeping vehicle keeps its last state, and its wheels theirs, with their spin 0.

fields.name: forwardSpeed
fields.doc: m/s along the chassis's -Z (forward), signed.

fields.name: gear
fields.doc: The engaged gear, numbered as VehicleInput::gear: -1 reverse, 0 neutral, 1..n forward. In Automatic the gearbox's own choice: it drops to neutral braking to a stop.

fields.name: clutch
fields.doc: The applied clutch, [0, 1], 0 engaged.

fields.name: shifting
fields.doc: Changing gear now.

fields.name: leanAngle
fields.doc: Motorcycle only: radians, + right.

fields.name: leftTrackSpeed
fields.doc: Tracked only: m/s.

fields.name: rightTrackSpeed
fields.doc: Tracked only: m/s.

types.name: Fenrir::Vehicle
types.doc:
Makes the entity's dynamic RigidBody a vehicle (ADR-0015): the body is its chassis, the only part of the vehicle that collides. Its wheels are VehicleWheel components on wheel entities of their own, each naming this entity. Chassis-local +Y is up and -Z is forward, by convention: turn a model facing another way on a child.

Game code drives it by writing `input` in `Tick`. With every default, a wheeled vehicle drives every wheel through an automatic five-speed gearbox.

Plain data that physics compares each tick with what it last applied (ADR-0011). A vehicle with no wheels is valid but inert. Its body needs a collider it can make, as any body does; the chassis must not be scaled to size its look: give it an unscaled BoxShape of the right size and a scaled look as a child.

Without a dynamic RigidBody with a solid collider, or beside a CharacterBody, it is inactive, with one warning each time it becomes so: a chassis turned kinematic or static, or losing its RigidBody or collider, is a plain body (if any), its `state` and its wheels' reset and its wheel entities left where they were. Valid again, it is built fresh with nothing carried over, so a car made kinematic for a cutscene restarts at idle in neutral.

Respawning is a Transform write: a teleport keeps the engine speed and wheel spin, as a body's velocity is kept, and the wheels are posed on the chassis's new pose at once. A rebuild (a wheel added, removed or relinked, or the chassis's body rebuilt in one tick, as when its collider is swapped) keeps the engine speed, the gear and each remaining wheel's spin; a new wheel starts still. A change to the chassis's scale moves the wheels with it, with no rebuild.

What is ground is decided by layers alone: each wheel's probe filters as the chassis's CollisionFilter does, finding only what the chassis would collide with, and never a trigger, the chassis itself or a character. Probes ignore joints, as queries do, so a joint's `collideConnected` never hides ground. A character is never ground: a vehicle meets one with its chassis, as an immovable wall, and to roll over something make it a dynamic or static body. A character pushes the chassis with its CharacterBody::pushForce, as it pushes any body, which barely moves a car, and one standing on the chassis rides it and presses on it with its weight. A wheel on a dynamic body pushes, loads and wakes it; on moving ground its slip is measured against the ground's velocity, so a vehicle parked on a kinematic platform rides it through tyre grip. Over light dynamic bodies the chassis dips: an artifact of the solver's mass ratio.

Only the chassis collides: queries and contact events see its body and name its entity, a body falling onto a wheel passes through it to the chassis, and QueryFilter::ignoreBody takes the chassis entity to skip the vehicle.

Parking is the handbrake: a vehicle at rest falls asleep as any body does, but never while `forward` is held or its engine is above idle. Asleep, it keeps its last `state`, its wheels' spin 0. Any change to `input`, any edit to a vehicle component (Vehicle, VehicleWheel, VehicleDifferential, VehicleAntiRollBar) and any rebuild wake the chassis, so pressing the throttle always drives. Stated cost: registering any vehicle stops the physics backend skipping its update of a world where everything sleeps, so a parked vehicle costs a little every tick.

Towing is an ordinary Joint: a trailer is any dynamic body, usually a TrailerVehicle, joined to the chassis, usually by a `ball` at the hitch. With the default `collideConnected = false` the hitch does not fight the chassis, and the joint links the two so they sleep and wake together. A wheeled vehicle given no input also tows, staying in neutral. Trailer brakes are game code's: copy the tractor's `brake` and `handbrake` into the trailer's `input` each tick; nothing links them. Stated limit: a trailer much heavier than its tractor jitters at the hitch.

Getting in and out is game code's: there is no seat component. To get in, set the character's CharacterBody::enabled to false, which hides it from bodies, queries, triggers and the wheels' probes, then parent its entity under the chassis (or a seat child of it) at a seat-local Transform. A disabled character is never posed by physics and never part of the chassis's compound (ADR-0014), so it rides along at the chassis's interpolated pose. To get out, unparent it and write its world pose beside the door, clear it of the chassis and anything else with PhysicsWorld::Depenetrate (or move it there with MoveCast), then enable it again.

Flipped and stuck vehicles are game code's too: there is no helper. Notice `state.wheelsOnGround == 0` with the chassis's up turned well away from world up for a while, then right it with a Transform write (upright, a little higher, its velocities zeroed) or a torque. A `maxTilt` of about 60° stops rollovers altogether.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: The kind and its drivetrain: WheeledVehicle by default.

fields.name: probe
fields.doc: How every wheel finds the ground. A live edit: the next step probes the new way.

fields.name: maxTilt
fields.doc: Radians: the cone around world up the chassis cannot pitch or roll past, a live edit. π (the default) is off; about 60° stops rollovers. Kept within 0 to π.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Disabled, the entity is a plain rigid body resting on its chassis, its `state` and its wheels' reset and its wheel entities left where they were. Enabled again, it is built fresh with nothing carried over.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: Read-back: overwritten by physics after every step.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleAntiRollBar
types.doc:
An anti-roll bar: stops a vehicle leaning in corners by pushing its two wheels' suspensions towards the same compression, on any entity. A vehicle has none by default. It works only while both wheels are on the ground.

A wheel that is not a wheel entity, or wheels of two different vehicles, make it inactive, with a warning, until its wheels are fixed; with a wheel empty it does nothing. A wheel that dies while named (its entity destroyed, or its VehicleWheel removed) is treated as empty, with one warning. Edits apply on the next tick and wake the chassis.

fields.name: leftWheel
fields.doc: A wheel entity, usually on the vehicle's left.

fields.name: rightWheel
fields.doc: A wheel entity of the same vehicle, usually the left wheel's partner on the right.

fields.name: stiffness
fields.doc: N/m: the push per metre of difference in the two wheels' compression. 0 does nothing.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleDifferential
types.doc:
A differential: shares a vehicle's engine torque between two of its wheels (or gives one wheel its share), on any entity. A vehicle with no differential naming its wheels drives every wheel equally; adding any differential replaces that, and a wheel in no differential only rolls and brakes. A rear-wheel-drive car is one differential naming its two rear wheels.

An empty wheel is "none", so a differential naming one wheel drives just that wheel. A wheel that is not a wheel entity, or wheels of two different vehicles, make it inactive, with a warning, until its wheels are fixed. Edits apply on the next tick and wake the chassis.

A wheel that dies while named (its entity destroyed, or its VehicleWheel removed) is treated as empty, with one warning: a rear-wheel-drive car that loses a rear wheel drives the other. Limit: a differential left with no live wheel names no vehicle, so if it was its vehicle's only differential, the vehicle drives every wheel again.

fields.name: leftWheel
fields.doc: A wheel entity, or empty for none.

fields.name: rightWheel
fields.doc: A wheel entity of the same vehicle, or empty for none.

fields.name: ratio
fields.doc: The gearbox's turns per turn of the wheels.

fields.name: leftRightSplit
fields.doc: How the torque is split across the two wheels: 0 all left, 0.5 even, 1 all right.

fields.name: limitedSlipRatio
fields.doc: The fastest wheel's speed over the slowest's past which all the torque goes to the slower one: above 1. A very large value is an open differential.

fields.name: torqueShare
fields.doc: This differential's share of the engine torque, against the other differentials of its vehicle: the shares are normalised, so they need not sum to 1.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleSuspension
types.doc: A wheel's suspension: how far it can rise, and how hard it pushes back.

fields.name: travel
fields.doc: Metres: the suspension travel, how far the wheel can rise from full extension. 0 is rigid.

fields.name: spring
fields.doc: The spring, in hertz and a damping ratio; a frequency of 0 is rigid. JointSpring's own damping default is 1.0, not the suspension's 0.5, so `.spring = {.frequency = 2.0f}` gives damping 1.0: write both.

fields.name: preload
fields.doc: Metres the spring is compressed at full extension, so it pushes from the start.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleTrackSide
types.doc: Which of a tracked vehicle's two tracks a wheel sits on.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleTyre
types.doc:
A tyre's friction against its slip: it rises from 0 at no slip to `peakFriction` at `peakSlip`, falls to `slideFriction` at `slideSlip`, and stays there. Along the wheel slip is a ratio, across it an angle in radians.

Grip on each surface: the curve's value combines with the ground's PhysicsMaterial::friction as the geometric mean, `sqrt(tyre * ground)`, as bodies combine theirs, so one `friction` means the same to bodies and tyres and ice, grass and tarmac need no surface table. The ground's friction is its body's material (a compound body's is its own entity's, or else its first collider's). Set ice very low: 0.05 under a 1.2 tyre still grips at 0.24. The chassis's own PhysicsMaterial plays no part: it is only what bodies touching the chassis feel.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleWheelState
types.doc:
How the last collision step left a wheel: written by physics into VehicleWheel::state after every step, from that collision step's probes against the chassis's pose after it, so contact, compression and steer lag one collision step. Game code's edits are overwritten. Off the ground, the ground fields are empty or 0.

A skid is game code's to judge: compare the slips with the tyre's `peakSlip` and `slideSlip`.

fields.name: groundBody
fields.doc: The body entity of the ground, on ground only. A handle: destroyed since, it is no longer valid.

fields.name: groundCollider
fields.doc: The collider entity of the ground touched, on ground only.

fields.name: contactPoint
fields.doc: World space.

fields.name: contactNormal
fields.doc: World space, unit length.

fields.name: groundVelocity
fields.doc: m/s, the ground's velocity at the contact.

fields.name: compression
fields.doc: Metres risen from full extension: 0 to `suspension.travel`.

fields.name: suspensionForce
fields.doc: Newtons.

fields.name: longitudinalSlip
fields.doc: Along the wheel, a ratio in VehicleTyre's terms.

fields.name: lateralSlip
fields.doc: Across the wheel, radians.

fields.name: angularVelocity
fields.doc: rad/s, + rolls forward.

fields.name: steerAngle
fields.doc: Radians, + right, as VehicleInput::steer.

types.name: Fenrir::VehicleWheel
types.doc:
One wheel of a vehicle, on its own wheel entity, naming the vehicle's chassis. It is never a body and nothing collides with it. Wheel order is entity order.

Physics poses the wheel entity for drawing: its world position and rotation (never its scale) are the chassis's pose times the wheel's own: `position` raised by its compression along the suspension, then turned by its camber and toe, then steered about the steering axis, then spun about its X, the axle. With no angle set its rotation is the chassis's, so left and right wheels can share a symmetric mesh. The Transform is output only: game code's writes to it are overwritten, and physics never reads a mount point from it. Keep wheel entities unscaled and out of the chassis's hierarchy, and give each a scaled look as a child.

Between ticks the wheels are interpolated with their chassis, under its RigidBody::interpolate and PhysicsConfig::interpolate, with no switch of their own: compression, steer and spin are blended between the last two steps, then posed on the chassis's blended pose, and `Tick` systems see the true pose. A teleported chassis or a rebuild snaps them. With the chassis not interpolated they are shown at their step poses.

Every setting is a live edit, applied on the next tick and waking the chassis. Out-of-range values are corrected with one warning per wheel: negative inertias, frictions, brake torques, travel and widths are treated as 0, the radius is raised to a small minimum, and `maxSteerAngle`, `caster`, `camber` and `toe` are kept below a quarter turn. Adding, removing or relinking a wheel rebuilds its vehicle. There is no per-wheel switch: destroy the wheel entity or unlink it to take the wheel off.

A wheel naming no other entity of its scene with a Vehicle, or sharing its entity with a RigidBody, a CharacterBody or any Collider (a trigger's included), is inactive: left out of its vehicle, with one warning each time it becomes so, and back by itself once valid. A Joint naming a wheel entity names no body.

fields.name: vehicle
fields.doc: The chassis entity: the entity with the Vehicle.

fields.name: position
fields.doc: Chassis-local metres from the chassis origin, scaled with the chassis: the wheel's centre at full extension.

fields.name: track
fields.doc: Tracked vehicles only.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc: Metres, never scaled.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Metres, never scaled.

fields.name: inertia
fields.doc: kg m².

fields.name: caster
fields.doc: Radians: + tilts the top of the suspension and steering axis back (+Z), as a motorcycle's fork.

fields.name: camber
fields.doc: Radians: + tilts the wheel's top outwards, away from the chassis's middle. Mirrored by the sign of `position.x`; a wheel at x = 0 counts as a right-hand one.

fields.name: toe
fields.doc: Radians: + turns the wheel's front inwards (toe-in). Mirrored by the sign of `position.x`; a wheel at x = 0 counts as a right-hand one.

fields.name: maxSteerAngle
fields.doc: Radians at full `steer`: 0 does not steer.

fields.name: maxBrakeTorque
fields.doc: Newton metres at full `brake`.

fields.name: maxHandbrakeTorque
fields.doc: Newton metres at full `handbrake`.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: Read-back: overwritten by physics after every step.
